clue.text: Possible place for pips

definitions.meaning: something likely to happen is said to be ...
the pips (suit symbols) of a pack are printed on playing cards

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for likely or probable is literally where the suit symbols sit, on playing cards.

clue.text: Northern ocean about freezing point — this will induce numbness

indicators.note: about means around, so the ocean's letters go round the freezing point

parts.note: the Arctic is the northern ocean
water freezes at zero degrees Celsius, shown as O

explanation.surface: Icy northern waters numb anyone who goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses and brings on stupor.

clue.text: "Cut!" the drover said

indicators.note: said means the name is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: Hugh the Drover is an opera by Vaughan Williams

explanation.surface: A cattle driver shouts an order to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hugh the Drover' is a Vaughan Williams opera, so 'the drover' is Hugh.
explanation.definitionFit: To hew is to cut with blows of an axe or sword.

clue.text: Man receiving medal, in first place

definitions.note: a phrase describing the winner; the answer is the noun for the person who is there

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the man's word holds the medal's letter

parts.note: a man is a chap
M is the abbreviation for medal

explanation.surface: A man is given a medal for winning.
explanation.definitionFit: A champ, short for champion, is the one who has finished first.

clue.text: Dissolute fellow not wanting commission

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man
off means not wanted, as in a dish that is off

explanation.surface: A debauched man turns down a job offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake-off is a share of profits taken, often illicitly, like a commission.

clue.text: Trace mobile calls in it

indicators.note: mobile means moving, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Police trace mobile phone calls made inside something.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny amount, a trace or spark.

clue.text: Edge slowly into church

parts.note: into gives the preposition in

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles cautiously into a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to advance by tiny degrees, edging forward slowly.

clue.text: Briefly, where you'd find best part of Brazil

definitions.meaning: summed up concisely, in a few words

definitions.text: where you'd find best part of Brazil
definitions.meaning: the kernel, the best part of a Brazil nut, lies inside its shell

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for concisely literally locates a nut's kernel inside its hard casing.

clue.text: Direction taken by fish, possibly

definitions.meaning: a stage of a meal, which may be the fish one

explanation.definitionFit: A course is both a route taken and one part of a meal, such as the fish.

clue.text: Catch footballer after indecisive game

indicators.note: after places the footballer's word behind the game's word

parts.note: a game with no winner is a draw
a back is a defending footballer, such as a full-back

explanation.surface: A defender scores after a stalemate in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a hidden snag or disadvantage, the sense of drawback.

clue.text: High-flier, one taking automobile to America

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
an automobile is a car
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A jet-setting traveller ships their car over to America.
explanation.walkthrough: Icarus is the boy of Greek myth who flew too near the sun on wings of wax.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical boy who flew with waxen wings is the archetypal high-flier.

clue.text: Bound to deprive sucker of one penny

indicators.note: to deprive the sucker of something is to take those letters away from it

parts.note: a lollipop is a sweet on a stick that is sucked
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A rule seems to require taking a child's lolly away for a single penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'obliged', but it is a verb: to move in leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to move with ungainly leaps, so it is a synonym of bound as a verb.

clue.text: Manipulation and massage realigned me

indicators.note: to massage figures is to rework them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A masseur realigns a client's back in a manipulation session.
explanation.definitionFit: Legerdemain is sleight of hand, deft manipulation by a conjuror.

clue.text: Angry words in unacceptable pop

parts.note: an idea that is out is no longer acceptable
to pop is to burst

explanation.surface: Someone shouts in anger at a song they find intolerable.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden outpouring of anger, such as a rant, is an outburst.

clue.text: Powerful force further repulsed by British servicemen — everything succeeded

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the word for further is read backwards

parts.note: again can mean further or moreover
the RAF is the Royal Air Force
everything is all
s is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Airmen beat back a strong enemy and win the day completely.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterfalls on the US-Canada border are an example of a powerful natural force.

clue.text: President's essential quality a few penetrate, but not artist

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: penetrate means get inside, so the trimmed word goes into the essential quality

parts.note: the root of something is its essential nature

indicators.note: but not means take away the artist from the word for a few

parts.note: several means a few
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A few people grasp what lies at the heart of a president, though no painter does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is just 'is' joining the definition to the rest; RA, a Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt were both US Presidents.

clue.text: Relation travelling from the east

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: A relative journeys here from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means of or from the East, especially Asia.

clue.text: Rejoin roadie on tour in long-haul holiday destination

indicators.note: a band on tour moves around, so these letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A band's road crew member is asked to come back to the tour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brazilian city is a far-flung holiday spot reached by a long flight.

clue.text: Regret carrying old codger up to entrance

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole assembly is read from bottom to top
carrying means holding, so the regret word holds the others

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a codger is an old man

explanation.surface: Someone regrets lugging an elderly chap to a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the whole assembly, as this is a down clue; 'entrance' is the verb, to charm, not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone, as a verb, is to captivate them, which is to enamour.

clue.text: Eastern time, Central European time, historical time, and so on

parts.note: CET is the abbreviation for Central European Time
an era is a period of history

explanation.surface: A list of time zones and periods that trails off without finishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means and the rest, used just like and so on.

clue.text: Makeshift bed puts everybody in a bad mood

indicators.note: in places the word for everybody inside the bad mood

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking
everybody is all

explanation.surface: Sleeping on a rough bed leaves the whole household grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pallet is a straw mattress or rough temporary bed.

clue.text: Tuck taken in simple attire

indicators.note: taken in means held inside the words simple attire

explanation.surface: A dress is taken in to make plain clothing fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold sewn into fabric, a type of tuck.

clue.text: Eight days of month with hail

parts.note: Oct is short for October
ave is the Latin greeting hail

explanation.surface: A week and a day in some month with hailstorms.
explanation.walkthrough: In church use an octave is the eight-day period after a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: In the church calendar an octave is a feast day plus the following seven, eight days in all.

clue.text: Patience perhaps demonstrated by potential to repeat

indicators.note: potential means latent or possible, so these letters could become something else

explanation.surface: Patience shows someone could do something again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patience' looks like the virtue, but it is the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, an example of a light opera.

clue.text: Sin, as defined by English bishop

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: An English bishop lays down what counts as sin.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to go astray morally, so it is to sin.

clue.text: Appear listless, loving Phoebe

definitions.meaning: to mope about dreamily, as if lovesick
Phoebe is a poetic name for the goddess of the night sky's lamp, and a satellite of Saturn

explanation.definitionFit: Phoebe is a classical name for the Moon goddess and lovesick mooning is listless dawdling.

clue.text: Tip over shot hawksbill, for instance

parts.note: a shot at something is a turn or go
the hawksbill is a kind of sea turtle

explanation.surface: Someone shoots a sea creature, which flips upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn turtle is an idiom for capsizing, like an upturned turtle on its back.
